chapter_title: Floor it! To the Golden City
title: Weekend Fever
subtitle: The disco ball and the pretty girl, get ready for a great time, friend!

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: Goood afternoon, San Francisco, to my dazed-out junkies, my loud and proud mischief-makers, and all my beautiful little heartthrobs!

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: It's your oldest and dearest friend, with the straight shooting of your father and tender-loving just like your mama. It's your boy, Vincent, aka "The Old Ostrich"!

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: Bringing you a balanced dish of good news and bad news! Let's soften the blow with the good stuff first: The New Age Market has finally gotten a little reinvigoration after the Harmonic Convergence.

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: Was it a sign from another world, or the harbinger of a Mayan doomsday prophecy? Who knows? But why worry, my lovelies? Keep those heads in the sand and your ears to the ground.

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: Because more visitors means more money! Huuuuge potential for young and old to make some dough!

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: Now, to hit you with the bad news—

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: Yesterday's gangland battles stretched from the sticks all the way to the steps of the People's Palace. And it came with a particularly heavy drizzle of bullet casings to rattle you all night long!

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: Last night, Legers the Dead and his arcanist minions booted the Tung Ch'ing Cham so hard in the ass, that they've been driven right out of our city!

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: If you're brave enough to head out into the streets, might still find a few gold teeth left on the ground!

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: Now, the sweet naive souls among you might think that means our fair city will finally have a moment of peace. But you listen to Papa Ostrich here, kiddies, this is only the beginning!

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: What Legers wants is nothing less than the whole damned city, and I have it on good authority where he's headed next.

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: I'm told his aim is to make a deal with Haight Street's very own Joe, aka "J Brown," for a stake in that juicy New Age Market pie.

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: Here's hoping that it goes smoothly, but if that fails, at least we'll have some quality entertainment.

items.speaker: Ostrich Radio
items.text: Now it's time for The Old Ostrich to duck his head again, leaving you with some solid music to grooove your body and shaaake your booty with our next track: The Golden City.

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: "Papa Ostrich," *sneer* give me a break—anyways, what can I get you, guy?

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Tequila.
Gio waves his hand, and the rest of his gang break off into the crowd.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: And ...
He pulls a bundle of notes from inside his jacket and puts it on the table.

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: Straight-forward. I like that.

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: So what are you after? The waitress's phone number, ticket to an underground boxing match, or you after someone specific?
The bartender's idle chatter digs under Gio's skin.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: You know what I'm after? I'm after you shutting your damned mouth!
He yanks the bartender by the collar, pulling him in close as he growls out his next words.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Cut the smart s**t with me and listen, 'cause I'm only going to ask once:

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: WHERE IS J? Point him out, then get your ass out of my sight!

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: Whoa, hey, hey! Easy, man! I'd be happy to; you don't even gotta tip me.

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: That bastard owes me money. So, you can go ahead and beat his ass, throw in a kick for me.
He drops the bartender's collar.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: You'd better not be playing with me, because that's a good way to get cut.

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: But, hey man, little heads up: J was born and raised in Haight Street, and he knows the place better than anyone. Ran circles around the cops. He won't be easy to corner.

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: Plus, he's got a lot of friends around, so picking a fight here could go south fast. Never know who's liable to stand beside him.
Gio's eyes narrow and dart around the room, but the bartender attempts to change the subject to calm things.

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: But you know what I say? The good times are over, so J and all his crew can bite the big one for all I care.

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: Hey, and uh, just so you know, you're the first one with enough guts to mess with him, so whether you're here to break his nose or ...

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: Well, this shot's on me, bro. To you, and your boss!
The clinking shot glasses at last break the ice, as a wry, wolfish grin escapes Gio's face.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Ha, you're a smart ass. We need more people like you.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Young guys these days are jammed by arcades and slots, you know. These adult children living in their mothers' basements. They ought to be out here begging for a job.
A heavy hand lands on the bartender's shoulder.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: What's your name, pal?

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: It's Vern, sir.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Put 'er there, Vern. Call me Gio.
Their hands clasp together in a hearty shake.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Alright, now you point me to this J bastard. And afterward, if you're looking to do some hustling, meet me at Rouge Street. I'll take you to the boss.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: But, uh, mind yourself around him, will ya? The old man's been unpredictable lately. Quick to fly off the handle, you know?

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: Thank you, sir, umm ...
The bartender moves to speak, tilting his head to one side.

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: I probably shouldn't pry, but, what do you want from J?

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: If you wanna take him down over Haight Street, you'll be disappointed. This place's got nothing but struggling folks. You couldn't mug someone for enough to catch the bus.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: What else could it be? That damn New Age Market. Don't know what Pops is planning to do with it, but he's got to have it.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Not like I'd give a damn otherwise. What kinda schmuck does business in a gutter like this?

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: But Pops' stubborn about it. Used to be I'd have a say in private, but he don't listen to anyone now except those freaks from the "Order of Enlightenment."

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Not that I'm crying about it, but robbing folks who ain't got no money, kicking 'em while they're down ... It don't sit right. But orders are orders.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: So, maybe I'll turn a blind eye, when I can.
The grin on his face goes sour, and he scans the bartender's face again.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: You ask too many questions.

items.speaker: Bartender
items.text: No worries, man. But you were looking for J, right? That guy in the suit, near the dance floor. See him?
Gio is already up and walking away before the bartender could finish.
His followers join him as he moves, advancing like hungry wolves toward their target.
The bartender drops his act, and with it, his smile turns fierce.
At the same moment, the silent woman stands up from another table and makes a graceful exit.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: See you later, J.
The bartender responds with an imperceptible nod.
Night Club
The technicolor lights cast everything in a dreamy glow.
Caught in the ecstasy of the pumping music, the dancers on the floor are unaware of the scene unfolding nearby.
The lead wolf fixes his gaze on his target and signals to his pack.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Three, two, one!
On his signal, they rush to the well-dressed gentleman.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Hold him down!
In a flurry of action, the gentleman is thrown from his seat down to the ground.
As the violence erupts, the crowded dance floor freezes, and the music stops on a skip.
Gentlemen, what is happening here?
Gio steps hard on the gentleman's shoulder, leaning down on him.
His face is twisted into a predator's smile.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Tie up his hands, but careful you don't break them, for now ...

items.speaker: "Dentist" I
items.text: Sure thing, Mr. Gio.
His grip tightens, veins bulging, and then—
*cracks*
The gentleman's hand pulls loose from his body, popping up through their grip and rolling across the floor.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: What the hell? What's going on with ... Huh?
An unseen hand taps Gio's shoulder. He turns his head.
"Pow!"—A heavy punch strikes him across the jaw.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Urrh!

items.speaker: J
items.text: That hurts. You got rocks in your jaw?
J shakes his bruising hand before extending it down to the mannequin gentleman on the floor.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Trust me, you're the perfect bait. You draw the fishes in like a magnet.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: I'm bait?

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: This is terribly unbecoming of you, J! Do you realize how many times this is? My body may be artificial, but my soul can feel pain, too!

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Heh heh. *spit*
Gio spits a gob of red from his bloody mouth.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: You lying sack of s**t.
He wipes his hand across his face, as he is helped up by his followers.
The lackeys all square up beside their leader.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Not so friendly after all, huh?

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: We'll continue our conversation later, J.
"Pop—"
Gio's dagger falls to the ground in a ringing clatter.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Now, who's lying, Mr. Gio? You took my shot, but you didn't even break that J guy's nose.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Still, thanks for the offer. Give my best to Mr. Legers for me.
Gio is beat, and he knows it.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Heh. The old man is gonna like you, smart ass.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: See you next time. We'll have another "parley," you and me.
He falls back toward the door flanked by his lackeys, before making a hasty exit.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Yeah, yeah, run on home with your tail between your legs. *spit* Legers's losers!

items.speaker: J
items.text: Looks like he might need a "Dentist," 'cause he just got kicked in the teeth!

items.speaker: J
items.text: They'll be home crying into their cereal soon enough! Haha!

items.speaker: J
items.text: The way they're hoofing it, they coulda outran my 4-cylinder Hummingbird G-R8100. They must have missed their calling. They ain't dentists. They're track stars.
The dance hall breaks into jeering laughter.
Bottles are raised and cheers made in recognition of their triumph.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Hahaha. Cheers! To unbreakable bonds!

items.speaker: All
items.text: To unbreakable bonds!
After a cascade of clinking glasses, the music is spun up once more, and the club returns to their dancing.
The excitement continues for some time after, only being broken by the arrival of a disheveled looking young man.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: Look, J, I gotta go. The shelter's gonna be closing up soon.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: My partner at the shop, you know ...
He rubs his stained-black fingers across his face, shaking off some flakes of drying blood.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: He doesn't like it when I come in covered with blood, scares the richie-rich types away.
It is getting late.
The celebratory atmosphere wears thin and tired as more people leave.

items.speaker: J
items.text: It's all good, bro. Thanks for coming today. If there's anything I can help ...
J pats his friend on the shoulder before pulling him into a hug.

items.speaker: J
items.text: You know where to go.
Hollick sniffs, returning the hug with a tight squeeze.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: Heh-heh. Thanks, bro. But, if you're really such a good friend ...

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: How about you spot me, a quarter mil- or so, so I can buy that sweet new convertible Lamberrari LM50. Since we're such good buddies, right?

items.speaker: J
items.text: Yeah, sure thing, buddy, right after I give you a knuckle sandwich, hahahaha.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: Hahahaha, see you around, J!
Waving off the mostly gentle giant, the rest of the group gathers around J.
Spirits are still high as they bask in today's victory.
But tomorrow, they must get back to work.
The moment shifts as a stumbling dummy drives a playful kick into J's leg.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Would you kindly give me back my damn hand already?

items.speaker: J
items.text: Hey, stop kicking me! Just a sec!

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: *panting*

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: M-my apologies. Where were my manners?

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Please don't take it personally, but I need to warn you that ...

items.speaker: J
items.text: Whoa, wait, wait! Someone's missing.
The disco ball continues its spin over the empty dance floor.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Where's Mercuria? Hey, Ms. Sputnik, have you seen her?
His eyes fix on the shining ball, which stops then descends from the ceiling to speak.

items.speaker: Sputnik
items.text: Oh, Ms. Mercuria? She left in a hurry, carrying that dagger those rough-type gentlemen dropped.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Do we follow her?

items.speaker: J
items.text: No, of course not.

items.speaker: J
items.text: She's just doing her thing.
He shrugs, looking out past the door.
Grimy Alleyway
Gio stumbles. He catches his breath before glancing back through the long alleyway.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: *panting* S**t! The old man didn't tell us what kind of mess we were in for here!

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: I'm not paid enough for this.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: *panting*

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Hey. Gio, right?
He stands unmoving, unblinking.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: You're just giving it back?

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: What's this meant to be, some kinda insult?

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Hey, y-your boss runs me off, now you're giving me back my own knife, like I'm some pity case? Think I won't hurt you 'cause you're a woman? Think again, b***h.
Anger overtakes his wariness of the woman, and he swings out his arm.
"Clink—"
The dagger drops to the ground as he reaches into his pocket, producing a wand.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: Vita Void!

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Umm ...

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: What is this?
The black arcane symbols dissolve in the air as soon as they touch her.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: The color of your energy is as dark as the coal in J's forge, no, worse, darker than I've ever seen before.
She jumps down from the fence and picks up the dagger.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: You're afraid. But something else besides that, I see a burning energy—the embers of a home reduced to ashes.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: A harrowing darkness that's followed you throughout your life, when your wife and child left you, when your debtors begged on their knees at your feet.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: W-what're you talking about?

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Huh, I understand you now, Mr. Gio. Forced to live with this darkness inside you.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Hmm.
She seems lost in her own thoughts.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: I'm sorry if I scared you, but I'm only here to return this.
She delicately places the dagger into his coat pocket. He shivers as if hit by a chill wind.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: You're a boy trembling inside this brawny shell of a man.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: You're too far down a path that you never wanted to set foot on, Mr. Gio.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: If you need help, find me in the New Age Market.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: *humming*
She hums softly, her steps light as she walks back from the dingy alley.
The man stands in place, lost in her words, until an alley cat leaps over his shoulder.
In his daze, he recalls the first time he fired a gun, the blood and brain matter, and the trembling midnight he spent hiding in the bathroom after.

items.speaker: Gio
items.text: *pukes*
